thread.title_full: President Trump exempts supersonic jet flights over Owyhee from water pollution rules

author: beaver state news
title: President Trump exempts supersonic jet flights over Owyhee from water pollution rules
text:
President Donald Trump announced this week that military supersonic jet flights over the Owyhee region are in the “paramount interest of the United States,” even if they result in river pollution and risks to fish.
The decision allows the U.S. Air Force to conduct combat jet training in a remote sagebrush desert shared by Oregon, Idaho, and Nevada without being subject to federal and local water regulations. This move comes two months into a war involving the U.S., Israel, and Iran.
Trump’s determination could undermine an ongoing lawsuit filed three years ago that seeks to limit these flights, which have caused loud sonic booms across the landscape. As part of their training operations, pilots release flares and clouds of aluminum-coated fibers known as chaff—countermeasures designed for defense but also sources of small metal fragments that environmental advocates say harm native fish populations. The Clean Water Act allows such exemptions if granted by presidential authority due to national interest.
Craig Johnston, a law professor at Lewis & Clark College, said: “This makes their lawsuit almost impossible to win.” He added: “The U.S. Supreme Court has sent signals to the lower court in the last year that they’re going to take any claims of national security very, very seriously.”
The Oregon Natural Desert Association (ONDA), which brought forward the lawsuit, is considering its next steps after Trump’s action. The group argues that military activities threaten about 969,000 acres in southeastern Oregon’s Owyhee Canyonlands with flammable flares and toxic metals harmful to trout native to local rivers. Federal reviews state residual metals from chaff and flares are expected to be minimal and mostly non-toxic except at high levels.
Residents near Mountain Home Air Force Base—the center for these trainings—have raised concerns about noise disturbances from low-flying jets. Arnold Thomas, Vice Chair of the Shoshone-Paiute Tribes’ Duck Valley Indian Reservation located within this area, said: “They’ve not been good stewards.” Thomas worries about disruptions affecting wildlife cycles: “When that sonic boom goes off…that indicates to those that are hibernating that it’s time to wake up.” Tim Davis from Friends of the Owyhee questioned how visitors can find solitude with jets flying overhead at low altitudes.
Johnston noted this appears to be Trump’s first use of a Clean Water Act provision allowing such exemptions for waterways on grounds of national interest—a power invoked fewer than a dozen times historically—and observed: “Certainly this administration seems more eager to use this power than any prior administration.”
summary: President Donald Trump announced this week that military supersonic jet flights over the Owyhee region are in the “paramount interest of the United States,” even if they result in river pollution and risks to fish. The decision allows the U.S. Air Force to conduct combat jet training in a remote sagebrush desert shared by Oregon, Idaho, and Nevada without being subject to federal and local water regulations. Trump’s determination could undermine an ongoing lawsuit filed three years ago that seeks to limit these flights, which have caused loud sonic booms across the landscape.
